quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: First up, Masai Ujiri hired as President of the Mavericks. I think this is a great hire for the Dallas franchise. Obviously, we know Masai can put together a championship team. We know he can draft talent, drafting a Scotty Barnes, drafting a Pascal Siakam amongst others. So, you know, we know he has an eye for making big trades and trading for a Kawai Leonard, making trades that most people wouldn't make, you know, and so, I think this is a great thing for the franchise, especially, you know, you're trying to navigate, you got Kyrie, you got Cooper Flag, uh, you know, where do you turn to next? I think they bring the right guy in and, you know, when he goes to these places, he has a lot of control. So, um, looking forward to seeing what Masai does in Dallas, but I think this is a great hire for their franchise.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green praises Masai Ujiri's potential impact on the Mavericks, highlighting his proven track record in drafting talent and executing impactful trades.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: You gotta give Rudy Gobert a lot of credit, man. Rudy Gobert been defending his ass off these playoffs. Put on a great performance for six games versus the Joker, uh, in the last series. And then he comes out Game 1 and he holds Wemby to 11 points on 17 shots. O for eight from the three, five for 17 from the field. That's incredible work, man. That's incredible work. I was a little worried about that matchup, but like I told y'all last pod, I says young fella, he knows his game. That means something. Can Wemby, I told y'all the story, can Wemby say, fuck you. I'm I'm done with you. I don't I I I I'm not not I'm done with you, but it has to be fuck you right now. It can't be no friends. I don't wanna talk to you. Don't talk fresh to me. Don't do none of that. We enemies right now. It has to be that. If not, you're gonna get big bro. That's just the way it goes. Gotta beat him.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green praises Rudy Gobert's defensive performance against Victor Wembanyama, highlighting his ability to limit Wemby's scoring and emphasizing the need for a competitive, 'fuck you' mentality in playoff matchups.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: But I'm gonna tell you another thing the Knicks have done that I think is very sustainable in this playoff run that takes a lot of pressure off Jalen Brunson and then just allow Jalen Brunson to get to it. Had 35 on 67% shooting last game. I think you can make it tough on Jalen Brunson if you overuse him and just have him trying to get it the whole time. I think you can put some guys on him that can make it a little tougher. The way you combat that, and I think what Mike Brown is doing a great job of, is you don't have him with the ball all the time. When it's time to get a bucket, when you're going in transition, yes, he's still getting to it. But he ain't just got the ball the whole possession. What they're doing, what's been great, is they're running the ball, the their offense through Cat, a little above the elbow, kind of out of a high split, you know, uh, Cat's flashing up, he's catching, and he's making all of the plays out of the high post. So then when Jalen Brunson get the ball, the whole defense ain't keyed in on him. You got OG coming off curls, like they've been running this kind of spread out offense with Cat, getting the ball at the high post, and Cat's been dropping dimes. Uh, he's been playing incredibly well. And I think that has unlocked other guys on this team. Also, you're not just, you're not overly relying on Cat being this 30-point a night scorer. But he's giving you that type of production, and it's very meaningful production, and it's also helping everyone else get off. And I think that's been the key, uh, to this Knicks group, man. It it's been looking beautiful.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green highlights the Knicks' effective strategy of running their offense through 'Cat' (likely a big man at the elbow) to alleviate pressure on Jalen Brunson, leading to more balanced scoring and unlocking other players.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: The Knicks destroyed the 76ers 137-98 in Game 1. And listen, this is the second game in a row that they have won by more than 39 points or more. That's no fluke. Uh, that's tough to do in the playoffs. Like you gotta give these guys a lot of credit. I think once they lost that game in Game 3, uh, where they let the game get away, uh, the Hawks came back, you know, it was kind of embarrassing the way they let that lead get away and the Hawks came back and won that game. And I just feel like after that game, they found something. Like, they've been pedal to the metal since. The defensive game plan, they've been dialed in defensively since. And that carried right over into, uh, this Philly series. Like they cover everything. They were trying to get the ball back to the pocket of Joel, they couldn't, the guard was jumping in the way, getting steals. They they throwing double teams at Joel. You know, it's causing turnovers, they're getting off to the races. And it ultimately really helped their offense, you know, and, you know, obviously led to a blowout.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green attributes the Knicks' dominant playoff performance, including two consecutive 39+ point wins, to a significant defensive adjustment and increased intensity following an embarrassing loss in their previous series.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Our last game of the night, the Thunder beat the Lakers 108-90. And Chet has his second straight double-double with 24 and 12. Listen, I think, like I told you all before, I think, uh, LeBron's going to have to guard Chet. I just think when his physicality, his smarts, uh, he'll be the only person on their roster that will be able to bother Chet at all. Uh, I love how they were sending the double team at Shai. They never really let Shai get into a crazy rhythm, but those guys got a great team, man, and they capitalized on that. I I did, um, speak about, you know, I thought this Lakers team would be better suited playing around LeBron because he's going to just slow it down. He ain't going to try to get in no pissing contest with the OKC Thunder. You know, and because of that, you know, it keeps turnovers low. Um, you know, it allows them to to keep it a half-court game as opposed to trying to get in this running game with the young OKC Thunder. And it was working.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green suggests LeBron James must guard Chet Holmgren due to his unique physicality and basketball IQ, and notes the Lakers' strategy of slowing the game down around LeBron to avoid a fast-paced contest with the young Thunder.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: I think this series is going to get a little spicy, uh, after VJ Ashcom's viral clip, uh, where he said that's all he's doing in regards to Jalen Brunson foul baiting. Listen, play clean defense, play physical defense, you know, drive, show your hands, meet him with your chest, they allow that type of physicality in the playoffs. You start getting your hands in there, it's tough. Get the get the big up to the level of the screen. This is where it gets tough with Joel guarding the ball screen with Jalen Brunson. Jalen Brunson come off, Joel don't get all the way up to the level of the screen. Jason Jalen Brunson come off, he put that guard in jail. Now he take off, the guard go to he he do all that that type of stuff. So, the only way to combat that is to get your guys up to the level of the screen. Now, I said before, you may have to put Joel on a different guy. You may have to have Joel really guard Josh Hart and live with Josh Hart shooting the three, because you gotta put somebody else in that pick and roll with Cat and you gotta put somebody that's gonna be up at the level of the screen. If you're not up at the level of the screen with you be up at the level of the screen with Drummond, you be up at the level of the screen if Bamba plays. But on Cat, I told y'all, man, PG may have to take on that responsibility, because it's not that he can't stop Cat from scoring. It's that all the other things and actions that they've been get into that puts Joel at a disadvantage defensively. So, uh, that is one of the ways that you can help yourselves, VJ Ashcom and the Sixers with the with the foul baiting, if you will, um, get up to the level of the screen. So he don't have the angles to come off, get you on his back and do all the trickery.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green predicts the Sixers-Knicks series will become 'spicy' due to comments about Jalen Brunson's foul baiting and offers tactical advice for guarding Brunson, suggesting Joel Embiid might need to be assigned to a different player to avoid defensive disadvantages.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Joel Embiid also took offense to Michael Bridges running into his side where he got the appendectomy. He said postgame, I don't know if it was dirty or not. I don't think it was necessary, but we move on. It's whatever, it's playoff basketball. I guess we gotta be more physical too and do it too. And I would say to Joel, absolutely, you most definitely do. Um, I'm not mad at Michael Bridges for doing that because if you're not healthy, you shouldn't be on the court. And as a defender, um, if you know a guy got an injury, you know, everybody got mad at Dillon Brooks last year with Steph. And I'm like, I can't I can't get mad at that. If you know a guy got a bad thumb, you're gonna hit that thumb. That's just the way it goes. That's been going on for years and years and years in the NBA. It's gonna go on for years and years longer. That's just the way it goes. You let someone know you have an injury, which is a lot of times, I try not to report all my injuries, because you let somebody know you have an injury, they're going to attack that injury. So, it's unfortunate, uh, and appendectomy is a pretty serious surgery, but can't blame Michael Bridges, you know, to me, listen, he ran directly into him. He didn't try to he dodge it, he ran dead smack into him. So, is it dirty? No, I wouldn't say it's dirty. Uh, is it intentional? I do think it's intentional.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green discusses the physicality of playoff basketball in the context of Joel Embiid's appendectomy injury, stating that players will target known injuries and that if a player isn't healthy, they shouldn't be on the court.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Knicks fans, I saw y'all after Game 1. I saw y'all got JR surrounded and all this stuff. I'm just saying, you cannot celebrate these things like this. I've told this to y'all before. You'll have a parade after you win a second round. How you gonna win the conference finals? We had the parade already. So I'm just telling y'all, Knicks fans, I know that it's been a rough go, and I know it's taken a while. Um, but don't blow it, because you're making it about yourselves and your tough journey. And I'll I'll I'll tell you a little secret, Knicks fans. Those current players don't give a fuck about your journey before. They don't give a damn that all of those teams before was getting their asses kicked. Those current players that it wasn't them, they don't give a damn. So, stop celebrating, you know, and doing this about for yourselves, Knicks fans. Game ends, go to a bar, go home, go drink, go do whatever you're gonna do, but stop having these melees and these parades outside of the Garden, man. You like, how do you keep your team hungry if you're having a parade for second round wins? Y'all y'all gotta stop this, man! I don't know how to tell y'all to be winning fans, but act like you're winning fans. Act like you've been there before, Knicks fans.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green criticizes Knicks fans for premature celebrations after Game 1 wins, arguing that such behavior can detract from the team's focus and hunger for deeper playoff success.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Another thing I I I think, uh, the Cavs are going to have to adjust is Cade Cunningham is going to have his way with Dean Wade. Uh, I'm not sure how much you're going to be able to play Sam Merrill. Uh, Dennis Schroder probably should get all of those minutes. Um, but I I I you may have to switch Dean Wade out of that start lineup and go Tyson because Dean Wade don't stand a chance against Cade. Uh, he gonna have a rough go. Uh, and Cade, 23 and 7, not nothing crazy, but he was just so in a rhythm and like everything was just so easy. You know, he got those dimes, uh, in the fourth quarter to stop the run and get Jalen Duren going just because like there was no he was unfazed by Dean. Like there's no pressure. He getting downhill, up, up, you know, drop off, up, boom, like, lefty, like, you know, I I just think he was so unbothered by Dean Wade. And I don't know that that's going to be the answer. So, they're going to have to take a look at that, uh, matchup. I I don't love that matchup.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green suggests the Cavaliers need to make significant lineup adjustments, possibly benching Dean Wade, as Cade Cunningham was 'unbothered' by his defense and easily dominated the matchup in Game 1.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: I love the way they moved Wemby around. They did not leave him just in one spot so he could wreck the defense. Sometimes he was on the wing, uh, having to be in the shell, sometimes he was on the block. Like they were moving, they brought him into actions and screen, like they and another thing that I thought was brilliant. Most people say, yo, let's, uh, let's space out to get Wemby away from the rim. And so we need to space out to the three. The Minnesota Timberwolves did something completely opposite, which I thought was incredible. They kept a guy in the dunker the whole time. And anytime they were in the dunker, they were engaging Wemby's body. They were ducking in, even if they weren't getting the ball, they were ducking in. So now a drive happens and they got him sealed off, they were just getting layups. I thought that was brilliant by the Minnesota Timberwolves. Would love to see how the San Antonio Spurs are gonna combat that. But the Minnesota Timberwolves have found something with putting him in that dunker and ducking him in every play. Because he couldn't get off and although he was blocking shots in the first half, remember he had what, nine in the first half or something like that. Second half, they was ducking him in, he couldn't get to it. And he was exhausted. Wemby seemed to be tired, uh, last night, man. He what didn't have that same defensive activity in the second half that he did the first half.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green praises the Timberwolves' brilliant game plan against Victor Wembanyama, noting their strategy of keeping a player in the dunker spot to engage Wemby's body and tire him out, leading to easy layups and reduced defensive impact.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Ant Man returned to for the first game of the series. He had 18 on 62% shooting in 25 minutes, 11 points in the fourth quarter. Uh, Mr. Clutch himself, didn't win the clutch award, but has been very clutch. Uh, listen, when Ant Man is on the floor or available, it just does something else for the confidence. And I gotta take my hat off to him. Uh, he he played an incredible game. I think the thing that y'all tend to forget is Ant Man really ain't played much in the last two months. You know, he missed most of the last 20 games of the season or 15 games or whatever it was. Played in a couple games last series. He hasn't played much basketball over the last two months. To see him have that type of rhythm, I thought was impressive. To see him gut through it, you saw him grabbing at the knee a few times. I thought it was impressive. But shout out to Jaden McDaniels. Jaden McDaniels has taken his game to another level on the offensive end since Ant Man has been hampered, and he's continuing to show that confidence. And I think that's making all the difference. And also get that young fella Terrence Shannon Jr. credit. Young fella shot out of a cannon and he going to the rack every single time. Probably had a couple layups that should have been called goal tends. Uh, but I love what he said after the game. He said he gonna have to keep blocking it because I'm gonna keep going. And if you got a coach that got confidence in you and telling you to keep going and keep going at his chest, you keep doing that. So the young fella been a good X-factor for them. And, you know, I love I love watching his growth.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green praises Anthony Edwards' impactful return despite recent inactivity, and highlights the impressive offensive growth of Jaden McDaniels and the aggressive play of Terrence Shannon Jr. as key factors for the Timberwolves.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: And it was working and then they had that stretch where they started turning the ball over. And once they started turning the ball over, those are going to be layups or threes. And so, gotta keep the turnovers down. Uh, felt like those happened at times where Bron was in the corner and off the ball. But any chance, man, if they want any chance, Bron has to man the game the whole game. If he doesn't, they won't have much chance. You lose by 18 points and Shai have 18 points. That's a tough one, you know. So, uh, I think their depth is far too much for the Lakers to handle. Um, but, you know, LeBron looks comfortable. Like I they're not going to do nothing to speed him up. He'll be fine. Uh, he can get those guys into the things that he want to get into, but you cannot have those stretches of turnovers because those are points. And, you know, when you make mistakes against OKC, they make you capitalize. It reminds me of the old Spurs teams. So, you know, they got to play as I said before, they they they got to play a perfect game to win. And I don't see a perfect game in the near future.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green emphasizes the Lakers' critical need to minimize turnovers against the Thunder, as mistakes directly lead to easy points for OKC, and suggests LeBron James must control the game entirely for the Lakers to have a chance.
